arxiv-2404-11397.title: Robust parameter estimation within minutes on gravitational wave signals from binary neutron star inspirals
arxiv-2404-11397.creator: Thibeau Wouters, Peter T. H. Pang, Tim Dietrich, Chris Van Den Broeck
arxiv-2404-11397.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Thibeau Wouters, Peter T. H. Pang, Tim Dietrich, Chris Van Den Broeck. The gravitational waves emitted by binary neutron star inspirals contain information on nuclear matter above saturation density. However, extracting this information and conducting parameter estimation remains a computationally challenging and expensive task. introduced Jim [ 123 ] , a parameter estimation pipeline that combines relative binning and jax features such as hardware acceleration and automatic differentiation into a normalizing flow-enhanced sampler for gravitational waves from BBH ( BBH ) mergers.

arxiv-2406-10486.title: Do Large Language Models Discriminate in Hiring Decisions on the Basis of Race, Ethnicity, and Gender?
arxiv-2406-10486.creator: Haozhe An Christabel Acquaye Colin Kai Wang Zongxia Li Rachel Rudinger
arxiv-2406-10486.description: Abstract We examine whether large language models (LLMs) exhibit race- and gender-based name discrimination in hiring decisions, similar to classic findings in the social sciences Bertrand and Mullainathan (2004) . We design a series of templatic prompts to LLMs to write an email to a named job applicant informing them of a hiring decision.

arxiv-2503-15782.title: High-throughput Discovery of Anti-gap Semiconductors
arxiv-2503-15782.creator: Zeyu Xiang, Fanghao Zhang, Bolin Liao
arxiv-2503-15782.description: Abstract Conventional semiconductors typically have bonding states near the valence band maximum (VBM) and antibonding states near the conduction band minimum (CBM). Semiconductors with the opposite electronic configuration, namely an antibonding VBM and a bonding CBM, are here termed “anti-gap semiconductors”. They have been theoretically proposed to exhibit excellent optoelectronic properties because of their strong tolerance to defects.

arxiv-2503-16071.title: Tuning LLMs by RAG Principles: Towards LLM-native Memory
arxiv-2503-16071.creator: Jiale Wei Shuchi Wu Ruochen Liu Xiang Ying Jingbo Shang Fangbo Tao
arxiv-2503-16071.description: Abstract Memory, additional information beyond the training of large language models (LLMs), is crucial to various real-world applications, such as personal assistant. The two mainstream solutions to incorporate memory into the generation process are long-context LLMs and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).

arxiv-2505-23947.title: Position: The Future of Bayesian Prediction Is Prior-Fitted
arxiv-2505-23947.creator: Samuel Müller, Arik Reuter, Noah Hollmann, David Rügamer, Frank Hutter
arxiv-2505-23947.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Samuel Müller, Arik Reuter, Noah Hollmann, David Rügamer, Frank Hutter. Training neural networks on randomly generated artificial datasets yields Bayesian models that capture the prior defined by the dataset-generating distribution. Prior-data Fitted Networks (PFNs) are a class of methods designed to leverage this insight. In an era of rapidly increasing computational resources for pre-training and a near stagnation in the generation of new real-world data in many applications, PFNs are poised to play a more important role across a wide range of applications.

arxiv-2509-11766.title: Igniting VLMs toward the Embodied Space
arxiv-2509-11766.creator: Andy Zhai, Brae Liu, Bruno Fang, Chalse Cai, Ellie Ma, Ethan Yin, Hao Wang, Hugo Zhou, James Wang, Lights Shi, Lucy Liang, Make Wang, Qian Wang, Roy Gan, Ryan Yu, Shalfun Li, Starrick Liu, Sylas Chen, Vincent Chen, Zach Xu
arxiv-2509-11766.description: Abstract While foundation models show remarkable progress in language and vision, existing vision-language models (VLMs) still have limited spatial and embodiment understanding. Transferring VLMs to embodied domains reveals fundamental mismatches between modalities, pretraining distributions, and training objectives, leaving action comprehension and generation as a central bottleneck on the path to AGI.

pmc-12581043.creator: Patrizia Brunner, Prateek Havanur, Steffeni Papukchieva, Benjamin Friedrich, Focke Ziemssen
pmc-12581043.description: ObjectiveIntravitreal antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy is the standard treatment for neovascular age-related macular degeneration and other retinal vascular diseases. This study aimed to assess therapy continuity in routine practice using pharmacy-based dispensing data in Germany, focusing on treatment with prefilled syringes (PFS).
